title: Exact mixing certificates for small positive Markov chains
statement: Given a rational row-stochastic matrix P of order 2 <= n <= 6 with every entry positive and every reduced denominator at most 100, compute its stationary probability row vector pi and tau = max_(i,j) (1/2) sum_k |P_ik-P_jk|. Certify d(t) = max_i ||P^t(i,.)-pi||_TV <= tau^t for every integer t >= 1, and return an integer T >= 1 with tau^T <= 1/100. Supply exact row-coupling certificates and a general argument, not only sampled trajectories.
status_basis: The cited textbook gives the coupling and submultiplicativity facts from which the stated certificate follows. Matrix-size, denominator and tolerance limits are curator-defined calibration conditions.
plain_summary: Turn a small exact transition matrix into a checkable guarantee on how quickly its probability distributions approach equilibrium.
assumptions: The input is an n-by-n rational matrix, 2 <= n <= 6, with positive entries, row sums exactly one and reduced denominators at most 100.
Time is discrete; row distributions evolve as mu P.
Total variation is one half of the sum of absolute coordinate differences.
The target bound concerns every integer t >= 1; the fixed tolerance is 1/100. If tau=0, T=1 is admissible.
scope: Individual matrices satisfying the stated bounds. Strict positivity avoids reducibility, periodicity and a one-step coefficient equal to one; sparse chains require a separately specified extension.
target: An exact certificate package for stationarity, maximal one-step couplings, the contraction factor and an integer mixing bound.
success_criteria: Verify positivity, rational input limits and stochastic row sums exactly.
Return a nonnegative normalized row vector pi with pi P=pi and explain uniqueness under strict positivity.
Provide a rational coupling for each pair of rows with the correct marginals and mismatch probability equal to their total variation distance.
Prove the all-time inequality using the source's submultiplicativity or a coalescing coupling, then certify tau^T <= 1/100 with rational arithmetic.
known_results: The textbook's Lemmas 4.11-4.12 bound distance to equilibrium by a submultiplicative pairwise distance; Proposition 4.7 and Corollary 5.3 give the coupling route.
prerequisites: Finite Markov chains and stationary distributions
Exact linear algebra and probability couplings
significance: A compact bridge between probabilistic arguments and exact certificates. It tests whether an assistant distinguishes a rigorous uniform bound from simulation-based evidence.

requirements.experiment: No physical experiment or stochastic simulation is required.
requirements.data: An explicit rational transition matrix; no observed trajectories or external data.
requirements.compute: Rational linear algebra on matrices of order at most 6 and coupling tables of order at most 6 by 6. Rational bit lengths can grow when certifying large T; resource estimates should be recorded for selected inputs before execution.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: A finite homogeneous discrete-time Markov chain with a strictly positive stochastic matrix. This is a model-internal assertion, not an estimate of an unknown transition law.

ai_assessment.rationale: The proof decomposes into established coupling facts and exact arithmetic checks. Small input dimensions allow independent review while retaining an all-time probabilistic claim.

clarity.reason: The admissible matrix class, norm and required inequality are specified.

decomposability.reason: Input checking, stationarity, couplings and the infinite-time argument are separable.

methods.reason: The inspected textbook supplies both coupling and submultiplicativity approaches.

search_or_symbolic.reason: Linear systems and finite couplings admit rational certificates.

checkability.reason: A second exact checker can verify the finite objects; the short general argument is reviewable.

expertise.reason: Stationarity and coupling must be interpreted correctly; simulation intuition is insufficient.

significance.reason: The bound is known and may be loose; the task mainly develops trustworthy probabilistic tools.

verification_difficulty.reason: The main risk is mistaking several checked times for an all-time proof or mixing up row and column conventions.

ai_assessment.uncertainty: No model has been tested. A compact matrix does not ensure a sharp bound or small rational intermediates.
ai_assessment.model_scope: No named model evaluated; assumes tool-using AI with finite probability, coupling arguments and exact rational computation.

obstacles: The coefficient can be close to one, giving a conservative bound.
Floating-point stationarity residuals do not prove exact stationarity.
A coupling must have the specified marginals at each step and remain together after meeting if the coalescence argument is used.

steps: Check every input constraint and the row-distribution convention.
Recompute pi P, normalization and nonnegativity with exact fractions.
Verify row-coupling marginal sums and mismatch probabilities independently.
Review the induction or coupling argument for all integer times and check the final rational inequality at T.
validation.human_review_difficulty: Moderate: finite arithmetic is straightforward; the passage from one-step certificates to all times needs a probability-trained reviewer.
validation.statement_alignment: The textbook applies broadly; the bounded task deliberately assumes strict positivity. It does not claim the displayed upper bound is the exact mixing time or infer P from data.

known_attempts: The cited text presents the underlying classical arguments. No specific matrix output is asserted here.
unresolved_checks: Choose representative matrices, including identical-row and slowly contracting examples, before making performance comparisons.
Any extension to chains with zero entries needs a new irreducibility, aperiodicity and multi-step analysis.

attribution.citation: Levin, Peres and Wilmer (2009), Markov Chains and Mixing Times, first edition, Chapter 4 and Sections 5.1-5.2. Input limits and certificate packaging are editorial choices.
attribution.curator_credit: Compiled for Theory Research Atlas with AI assistance.

status_search.result: The contraction tools are established textbook results. This card specifies a bounded exact reproduction.
status_search.limitations: No claim is made about optimal mixing-time estimation, all later refinements or actual solver performance.

epistemic_layers.formal_validity: Certificates and proof must establish the bound for the exact supplied matrix.
epistemic_layers.empirical_support: Applying the bound to measured systems would require separate evidence that their transition law is adequately represented by this fixed matrix.

correctness.basis: No candidate answer has been submitted or independently reviewed.
